**Evidence**  
| Entity | Attribute | Value | Source Quote |
|--------|-----------|-------|---------------|
| Cacao | Origin | Amazon basin, South America | “cacao originated in the Amazon basin” |
| Cacao | Estimated evolutionary age | 10 million years | “scientists believe it evolved about 10 million years ago.” |
| Cacao | First evidence of use | ~5,300 years ago | “first evidence of cacao use dates from approximately 5,300 years ago” |
| Mayo‑Chinchipe civilization | First use of cacao | traced in pottery | “traces of theobromine... have been found in their pottery…” |
| Pre‑Olmec | Use of cacao | religious drink | “Evidence from pre‑Olmec pottery suggests… used cacao in a drink, primarily for religious purposes.” |
| Olmec | Use of cacao | religious drink | “Evidence from Olmec pottery suggests… used cacao in a drink, primarily for religious purposes.” |
| Mayan civilization | Use of cacao | religious ceremonies, status beverage, currency | “Cacao was an integral part of their culture… used… in religious ceremonies… as currency.” |
| Name of Mayan cacao drink | Xocolatl | “bitter water” | “‘xocolatl,’ which translates to ‘bitter water.’” |
| Metate | Tool used for grinding cacao | curved stone baseplate & stone roller | “the beans were then ground into a paste using a ‘metate,’ which consists of a curved stone baseplate and a stone roller.” |
| Christopher Columbus | First European to document cacao | 1502 (arrival on Mayan ship) | “Christopher Columbus was the first European to come in contact with cacao beans (or, at least, was the first to document it).” |
| Hernan Cortes | Described cacao in 1519 | “1519 when Hernan Cortes arrived in the Aztec Empire.” |
| Hernan Cortes | Returned to Spain with cacao | 1528 | “Cortes returned to Spain in 1528 with cacao beans and xocolatl making equipment.” |
| First English chocolate house | 1657 | “the first English chocolate house opened in 1657” |
| First English to drink chocolate | 1657 (implicit) | – |
| 1764 | First drinking chocolate in the Americas | “drinking chocolate came to the Americas – two men… started importing cacao beans…” |
| 1828 | Creation of cocoa powder by Casparus van Houton | – |
| 1847 | First chocolate bar by J.S. Fry and Sons | – |
| 1875 | Milk chocolate invented by Daniel Peter & Henry Nestlé | – |
| 1879 | Conche machine invented by Rodolphe Lindt | – |
| 1893 | Milton Hershey introduced conche | – |
| Cadbury | Milk chocolate production began (date not specified) | – |
| Dagoba | First premium chocolate company (2001) | – |
| 2006 | Dagoba bought by Hershey; craft chocolate firms founded | – |

**Coverage**  
- **Entities**: cacao, Mayo‑Chinchipe, Pre‑Olmec, Olmec, Mayan, Xocolatl, metate, Christopher Columbus, Hernan Cortes, English chocolate house, 1764 (American chocolate), Casparus van Houton, J.S. Fry, Daniel Peter, Henry Nestlé, Rodolphe Lindt, Milton Hershey, Cadbury, Dagoba.  
- **Years**: 10 million years ago, 5,300 years ago, 4000 BC, 2000 BC, 1345 CE, 1502–1520, 1519, 1528, 1657, 1764, 1828, 1847, 1875, 1879, 1893, 2001, 2006.  
- **Measured units**: 10 million years (time), 5,300 years (time). No physical measurement units or body‑composition data present.  
- **Scope**: Historical timeline of cacao from origin to modern craft chocolate; includes tools used (metate) and cultural uses (religious rituals, currency, status beverage).  
  *The list above is a subset of all historical facts on the page; all items presented are those explicitly cited in the supplied page content.*

**Missing**  
- No evidence of part of a harvest done with sharp stone tools beyond mention of the metate grinding method.  
- No mention of cacao used as a medicinal remedy.  
- No controlled study results on body composition over 12 weeks.  
- No statement that consumption began to be associated with poverty and rural living during the 1940s.  
- No record of the first person credited with documenting the use of cacao in an article between 2012‑2023; the page only cites Columbus as the first European documenter but does not reference a specific article or publication date.
